title: Florida House, District 56
what_it_does: Represents District 56 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Incumbent Republican Brad Yeager faced Jessica Naioti in the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary; coverage stated a Democrat awaits in the general election. The News Service of Florida reported all 13 Republican incumbents with primary challengers won, which indicates Yeager advanced. The Democratic nominee's name was not found. (An earlier June 8 Florida Politics item listing Yeager as unopposed was superseded by qualifying.)
verified_ballot_note: Ballotpedia: 'Incumbent Brad Yeager and Jessica Naioti are running in the Republican primary for Florida House of Representatives District 56 on August 18, 2026' and a Democrat awaits in the general election (https://ballotpedia.org/Brad_Yeager); CBS Miami/NSF: all 16 House incumbents facing primary challengers won (https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/florida-house-senate-primary-election-results-2026/). Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

record.item: Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
Voted for SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted for HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted for HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted for SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.

Voted for SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

Voted for CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

candidates.name: Jose Freites
candidates.occupation: Activist and community organizer; self-described Democratic Socialist
candidates.background: Jose Freites describes himself as a lifelong Floridian, activist, community organizer and Democratic Socialist running 'to fight for the working class'. His site lists platform headings (environment, housing crisis, 'people over insurance profits', public safety, 'defending our neighbors', teachers) without detailed text as of Sept. 18, 2026, so no issue positions are coded. Endorsed by Pasco-Hernando DSA.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

housing.summary: Freites calls for amending the state constitution to protect the Sadowski affordable-housing trust fund, repealing Florida's statewide ban on rent control so local governments can set their own rules, adding anti-price-gouging limits on sudden rent increases, and building community-owned housing in Pasco County priced for teachers, nurses, first responders and service workers.

sources.title: Stop The Bleeding On The Housing Crisis - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

insurance.summary: Freites supports HB 30, which he describes as capping annual property-insurance increases at 10 to 15 percent, restoring one-way attorney fees when claims are wrongly denied, and requiring insurers to publicly account for premium increases.

sources.title: The People Over Insurance Profits - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

environment.summary: Freites says he would advance legislation strengthening protections for wetlands, springs and aquifer recharge areas against sprawl and large industrial water users, and argues current leaders talk about conservation without acting.

sources.title: Protecting Our Lands & Defending The Environment - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

growth.summary: Freites frames sprawl, large-scale warehouses and AI data centers as threats to Pasco's water and neighborhoods, and says he would restrict their expansion and strengthen legal defenses for recharge areas against them.

sources.title: Protecting Our Lands & Defending The Environment - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

energy.summary: Freites says he would restrict what he calls Big Tech data centers from driving up residents' electric bills, and ties utility costs to tighter oversight of large industrial power users.

sources.title: Protecting Our Lands & Defending The Environment - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

immigration.summary: Freites says he would end cooperation between local police and federal immigration agents, extend due-process protections to undocumented residents, and allow immigrant residents to obtain driver licenses and use public-safety services regardless of status.
immigration.quote: Our police officers should be in the field catching real criminals not racially profiling and terrorizing our migrant communities

sources.title: Defending Our Neighbors - All Of Them - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

education_choice.summary: Freites opposes expanding Florida's universal voucher program, saying it moves public-school money into private schools and mainly benefits wealthier families. He also calls for raising teacher base pay, restoring experience-based pay steps, repealing SB 256 and restoring binding arbitration for teacher unions.
education_choice.quote: We must oppose the universal school voucher system expansion as it will only divert public school money into private schools

sources.title: Fighting For Our Teachers - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

crime.summary: Freites would make mobile crisis teams pairing mental-health professionals with trained responders the default response to mental-health calls, fund crisis stabilization units as an alternative to jail or the emergency room, add oversight and due-process safeguards to Baker Act holds, and staff school-based mental health so students are helped before a situation becomes a disciplinary or criminal matter.

sources.title: Public Safety That Actually Keeps Us Safe - Jose Freites for Florida House 56

other_issues.title: Repealing classroom speech restrictions
other_issues.summary: Freites says he would repeal the Stop WOKE Act and related classroom restrictions, protect teachers' academic freedom, and remove personal liability for teachers and librarians acting in good faith.

sources.title: Fighting For Our Teachers - Jose Freites for Florida House 56
